data.content_ref: inline:SRC_002 asserts that the panel+checklist beats the expert ONLY on bias-susceptible tasks and 'never beats the expert' on bias-free tasks, but offers no causal mechanism for why checklist value is exclusively bias-suppression rather than also bias-reduction via adding valid cues. Its own analogy section explicitly flags this: 'A checklist can also add valid cues, not only suppress bias, conflating two mechanisms.' Yet the claim and mechanism section ignore this alternative mechanism entirely. If a checklist adds a valid cue the expert's intuition omits (e.g., a base-rate table the expert would not have retrieved), the panel can beat the expert on a bias-free task precisely because the expert's failure mode is a missing cue, not systematic bias. The interaction test (panel advantage only on bias-susceptible items) would misclassify this genuine reliability gain as 'something else' and incorrectly predict no panel advantage, even though the gain is real and causal. The target's 'only on' restriction is therefore unwarranted by its own stated disanalogy, and the proposed single-evaluation evidence is invalid against the alternative causal pathway the target itself acknowledges.
